speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; can you tell me exactly how long these symptoms have been present and how severe the fever is?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome), likely triggered by a prior infection (e.g., Chlamydia or Campylobacter) given the recent camping trip, history of self-resolving knee pain (suggesting preceding septic arthritis or reactive episode), and current presentation of monoarticular wrist pain, fever, and malaise.
